results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 76 aligned units' outline summaries state the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order; the 5 callouts match no spec paragraph and restate the thesis, stakes and failure patterns as the spec's introduction requires.

The outliner marked two units. Introduction ¶3 (p03): the spec's controlling idea itself joins the two owned terms with their application to Veldmark, and the Veldmark sentences are subordinate to the definitions. Worked Example ¶6 (p48): 'write load and value are inversely distributed' and 'cost models must be read against the profile' are the premise and consequence that the spec's single controlling idea for p48 states in one sentence. Neither unit holds an idea outside its spec paragraph.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: differences and the three breaking rows (V1), the four layers per capability part (V2), layer-1 requirements and the layer-2 test (V3), layer-3 ownership (V4), the stage gate and governance (V5); the conclusion synthesises the thesis and hands off.

Tables 1-8 and Figures 1-3 are each introduced and followed by a caption or paragraph that says what they show (e.g. Table 2 -> 'differ on almost every row', Table 7 -> factor of eight and the inverse distribution in ¶6, Table 8 -> its caption and the stage gate); the dated public sources and the AVIV/Adevinta quotations are each tied to the claim they support.

Every declared transition_in is present at its boundary with the declared relationship: e.g. p06 contrast ('three incompatible positions'), p07 problem_solution, section in-practice additional_support ('The row sections above cited the record one dimension at a time'), architecture cause_effect ('Verticals differ, outside parties rewrite their requirements ... so the answer is neither one platform nor none'), trade-offs contrast ('The four layers are one answer; a group could choose others'), failure-modes elaboration (callback to Felix's stage gate), chief-architect problem_solution, conclusion conclusion_summary ('This chapter opened with ...').

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Three Listings, Three Physics ¶1
results.quote: Veldmark's workshop applies the profile and the share test in three steps. In March it drafts the profiles from the listing each brand brought, and a first classification of the capability list. In April that classification is ratified (Table 8, at the end of this section). From March to May, Ingrid's team checks the profiles against the three listings
results.finding: Reader A (item 3.6): the 'three steps' overlap in time and the ratified result is announced before the work that leads to it, so the reader cannot tell whether the listings fed the classification until ¶8's 'tests it rather than shapes it'. The spec's timeline is sound; the prose calls overlapping activities 'steps' and points forward to Table 8 instead of stating up front that the March drafts and the April ratification precede the March-May checks the section then presents.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-b, item 3.1 (the worked example's three overlapping 'steps' and Table 8 announced before Tables 6 and 7; also its reordering suggestion 4.1)

results.quote: **Profiling only the largest vertical.** Felix's stage gate is the defense against the Forced Fit: a group platform built around one vertical's physics and imposed on the others. That is the first of six ways option B decays, and it starts when only the largest vertical is profiled.
results.finding: Reader A (item 3.9): the first failure mode opens with the previous section's remedy, redefines the Forced Fit and announces 'the first of six ways' mid-paragraph, so the section framing sits inside its first item under that item's label. Every does_not_know term is given at or before use where it matters: DMS ('dealer management system (DMS) feeds', scene), MLS and ATS expanded in Table 2, IDX glossed in Table 3, DPE as 'energy performance diagnostic (DPE)', ESCO as 'the EU's ESCO' occupation taxonomy, VIN as a 17-character identity decoded by vPIC, type-approval codes named with hsn/tsn; profile and share test defined in the introduction and Concepts. Pattern names reader B flagged (Ghost Inventory, Seeing Double, Deal-Shaped Architecture) are among the fifteen names the audience already knows. Neither flow reader reported an unexplained term otherwise.

The introduction opens with Part I's sameness and the synergy case's concrete question (sofa, car, apartment, job), states the thesis and the two owned terms, and gives a roadmap; no dictionary opening, throat-clearing or announcement-only pattern.

The conclusion answers the opening question, synthesises Part I, states the consequence and a course of action, and hands off to Part II; it neither merely repeats the body nor adds new material or apology.

¶1 gives the answer ('no for the listing model and yes for the machinery beneath it') and ties Part I's chapters into one share test; ¶2 gives the so-what (forum ratifies a table in April 2027 instead of arguing; Motorvane moves only when the engine meets its own feed success rate and delete latency) and the takeaway (write a numbered profile per vertical and place every capability part in a layer with an owner and a reason).

¶1 restates the opening question about the sofa, car, apartment and job and answers it; ¶2 calls back to Part I's opening claim that the business decides the architecture and turns it into a procedure, as the spec's callback requires.

The intro-only reader listed the nine stages in the roadmap's order (workshop; the two terms; five-vertical comparison; public record; outside parties; four-layer platform with seams; pure strategies; three Veldmark listings and the classification; failure modes, Chief Architect's view, review questions), the evidence (concrete item examples, the public record, fictional Veldmark) and a plain prescriptive tone. Gaps it noted (layers not all named, public cases not named, recommerce's place at Veldmark) do not miss any roadmap promise.

The AC-2 reader predicted the same nine sections in the same order as 'expected', and the evidence as concrete examples, the public record of groups that undid sharing, and the fictional Veldmark group. Its unclear points (unnamed public cases, layers named only through the key points, recommerce, which listings) are details the body supplies and do not contradict the expected answer.

The reader said the plan should not decide; the engine meeting the vertical's profile should, measured by Motorvane's own feed success rate and delete latency, made a stage gate. It placed the vehicle schema and DMS feed adapters as layer-2 vertical content on shared engines and 'vehicle identity, specification and price rating' as a layer-3 capability owned by Motorvane for the group. This matches 'expected'; its open points (no target numbers, who approves the gate) are beyond the criterion.
The independent reverse outline lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the spec's sections and paragraphs (76 of 76 aligned units match; callouts unmatched by design).
